_comment: Hand corrections applied on top of the OCR pass by tools/build_coords.py.
Board positions are in pixels of .build/a12/drawing_full.png (5265 x 3029);
schematic positions are in pixels of .build/a12/sch<N>_full.png. The builder
normalises both. Every entry here was measured by eye off a labelled pixel
grid over the full-resolution image and then checked by rendering the marker
_sheetImageSizeComment: The three sheets of Figure 7-14 were cropped separately and are not the same
size: sheet 2 is 1.2% wider than sheet 1 and 1.6% taller. One shared {w,h}
would put every hand-placed schematic marker a few pixels out, so each sheet
declares its own. Measured with 'magick identify' on .build/a12/sch<N>_full.png.
_boardComment: x,y is the centre of the silkscreen designator, w,h its extent. A12's
plotter typeface gives a three-character horizontal label about 110 x 50 px
and a vertical one about 50 x 115 px; four characters (CR14) about 155 px
along the text.
Test point entries span the label and its pad together: the pad is the short
bar drawn beside the TPn text, about 25 px to its right on this drawing, and
a marker centred on the text alone would send a probe to the wrong side of
the label.
The last sixteen entries are different in kind: they are the reader's own
positions, promoted. Every board marker was rendered and looked at, and the
nine the reader flagged as a collision and the seven it called ambiguous all
turned out to be right. A badge that keeps warning about a disagreement
somebody has settled is noise, so they are recorded here as checked. Two of
them were resized as well: CR13's box spanned 408 px and R57's 278 px, both
merged reads, and a marker that large is a poor probe target even when its
centre is right.
The rest fall into two groups. Some are parts the reader placed on a
neighbouring label -- almost always by truncation, C58 read as C38 or C88 as
C68, or by losing a leading letter, CR3 read as R3 and C40 read as C4. Those
carry a note saying what the reader had hit. The others are parts the reader
never found at all and that are plainly lettered on the drawing.

_dropComment: H5 is a rivet and has no silkscreen designator at all; the reader produced a
tall box over the VR2/R5 pair for it. A marker that points at another part's
label is worse than no marker, so it is dropped and H5 is listed as not on
_notOnDrawingComment: Parts in the list of replaceable parts that carry no silkscreen designator on
the assembly drawing: rivets, a screw, the board ejectors, the TO-8 heat
sink, the oscillator thermal cover, the high voltage control shield and a
soluble spacer. They stay in the parts list and remain searchable, but
counting them as unplaced would make the coverage badge lie.
_schematicComment: Hand placements on the schematic sheets, in pixels of the sheet named by the
key (see sheetImageSize). A hand entry replaces every read of that designator
on that sheet, so anything listed here need not also be dropped.
The test points are the reason this section exists. Every one is written twice
in the set: once in the legend box at the top of sheet 1, which lists all eight
with the sheet and zone where each flag is drawn, and once beside the flag
itself. The legend is crisp text in a neat column, so the reader prefers it, and
a marker on a legend row answers a question nobody asked. The legend's own zone
references say where each flag really is: TP1 (PG1C7), TP2 (PG1B8), TP3 (PG1C7),
TP4 (PG1C5), TP5 (PG1B1) are all on sheet 1, and TP6 (PG2D4), TP7 (PG2C3) and
TP8 (PG2C2) are all on sheet 2. So the TP6/TP7/TP8 markers the reader put on
sheet 1 are legend rows and are dropped, and the three are placed by hand on
sheet 2 against the signal name printed beside each flag.
The rest are parts that are genuinely drawn on the sheet but whose marker the
reader had put on some other text -- a part number, a caption, a note.

_dropSchematicComment: Schematic reads known to be wrong, reviewed marker by marker against the sheet.
Three kinds dominate, and all three are in the pitfalls list:
the transistor pinout legend at the right of sheet 1, captioned with the
designators it applies to -- Q12, Q13, Q14, Q20 are that block, and C18 and H5
are misreads of its 'Q16-Q18' caption and of a package pin letter;
a part number or net label read as a designator -- L2 and MP9 on 'TL072' and
'OP-07', Q7 on 'OP-07', C64 on 'DG444', C82/C84/C87 on the AD7534's DB pins;
a word in the notes block or a caption -- C2, L1, Q9, Z2 and U2 all landed in
H5, HS1, M12 and MP9 are hardware with no schematic symbol at all, so every read
of them on a sheet is wrong by construction.
_layersComment: Alignment of the photograph to board space. Twelve landmark pairs, each
one a designator whose silkscreen is legible in both images: C48 at the
top left, CR2 and R8 across the top, C68 and U9 down the right-hand side,
C87 at the left, C4, C18 and R68 along the bottom, C35 and C91 through the
middle, C69 up the left of centre.
This is the easiest of the three to align. Only the oscillator thermal
cover (M12) is fitted, over U14 and U16 at around x 0.21-0.37, y 0.33-0.51
in board space, and the landmarks bracket that patch on all four sides
rather than extrapolating into it.
The src side is not eyeballed: it is the reviewed board coordinate of that
designator from data/a12.coords.json, so it is the same point the markers
are drawn from. The dst side was not eyeballed either -- the locator
drawing is the silkscreen artwork, and the photograph shows that same
silkscreen in yellow ink, so the drawing patch around each designator was
cross-correlated against the photograph and each pair is a local
registration rather than a click on a pixel grid.
Fit residuals are 1.6 to 6.7 px on a 3000 px-wide drawing. Checked by
warping the photograph into board space and drawing the locator artwork
over it: the relays, the UCN5801A drivers, the 82C55, the Z5/Z6 networks
and both card-edge connectors sit on their outlines. Sampling the whole
board with the same correlation afterwards gives a median residual of 3.0
drawing px over 35 patches.
Marked approximate. The shot is not perfectly overhead, and the drawing
does not print every designator where the board does -- Fluke moved a lot
of the text inside the part outline for legibility -- so a landmark is the
drawing's position for that part, which is the position the marker uses,
not necessarily where the board's own text sits.
src is normalised in the drawing (3000 x 1726), dst in the photo
